claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on high-entropy-alloy crystal structures and thermal-conductivity values can accurately identify alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The predictive approach works by leveraging the interplay among lattice distortion, atomic disorder, and phonon scattering.
The target materials are high-entropy alloys in the as-cast state.
The machine-learning training dataset will contain at least 100 high-entropy alloys.
The training data will include alloys with varying compositions and crystal structures.
Model testing will use alloys that were not included in training.
Lattice distortion and atomic disorder are the structural mediators relevant to the prediction.
Lattice distortion and atomic disorder increase phonon scattering.
Increased phonon scattering reduces thermal conductivity.
The approach will improve predictive accuracy by 20% relative to current state-of-the-art thermal-conductivity models.
The approach will achieve a mean absolute error of 0.05 W/m-K.
The relevant baseline is current state-of-the-art predictive models for thermal conductivity.
The approach is applicable to high-entropy alloys having FCC or BCC crystal structures.
The approach is limited to alloys containing no more than five principal elements.
Model accuracy may depend on the quality and diversity of the training dataset.
Complexity in the underlying physical mechanisms may contribute to uncertainty in model accuracy.
The experimental benchmark will test 20 high-entropy alloys predicted by the model to have low phonon thermal conductivity.
Thermal conductivity will be measured at room temperature using the laser-flash method.
Crystal structures of the benchmark alloys will be characterized using X-ray diffraction.
The hypothesis will be falsified if the mean absolute error between predicted and measured thermal conductivity exceeds 0.10 W/m-K.
